Accepted: 'Mission mission' is declared at input.c:272 under '#ifdef PLATFORM_PS4' (:266) and at :282 under '#ifdef PLATFORM_XBOX' (:278), in two consecutive blocks; the detector treats only the arms of one #ifdef/#else as exclusive. Neither block compiles in a PC build.

Accepted: the '#ifdef ENABLE_LOGGING' block at bunkerbroadcasthandler.c:338-340, inside a method, holds only a comment. Bohemia documents ENABLE_LOGGING as set by -doScriptLogs=1 (1_core/defines.c:36-39); the dayz-mcp v1.4 release game ran without it and without a crash. With the macro set, the block is not measured.

Accepted: the '#ifdef DIAG_DEVELOPER' block at environment.c:1-3 holds only a comment. DayZDiag defines DIAG_DEVELOPER on server and client (the dayz-mcp v1.4 release game, DayZDiag 1.30.164078, 2026-10-17, logged its DIAG_DEVELOPER-only plugin on both), and that game ran this file without a crash, so the segfault that pitfalls-advanced.md:66 describes did not happen here. The rule stays live for mods until that claim is measured again (A2).

measured.roots: P:\scripts on the owner's PC (DayZ 1.30.164078 stable); the --update run and the check after it gave the same findings and the same digest

tree.dayz_build_note: Build of the measured tree: DayZ 1.30.164078 stable (DayZDiag_x64.exe product version 1.30.164078.38). sources/source-map.json declares the build the pack is anchored on, which can be older. Identity of the control tree is the digest; set this deliberately when re-baselining after a patch.
tree.digest_scope: sha256 over (posix relpath, sha256 of contents) of every file the validator discovers under the vanilla root, in walk order. Not comparable to the vanilla_index digest, which covers .c only.

what_this_is: Expected findings of dayz-script-validator over Bohemia's vanilla script tree. The tree compiles and ships, so any finding on it is a false positive by construction: this file is the allowlist of the ones already triaged, each with the reason it is tolerated. A finding that is NOT here fails the control.
